label: Workers who drove alone to work (%)
definition: Workers 16+ who usually drove alone in a car, truck or van as a share of all workers 16+ (denominator includes people who worked from home).
breaks: Line definition unchanged; work-from-home growth in periods that include 2020 onward lowers shares of other modes
limitations: Usual mode in the reference week; large MOEs for tracts and block groups; resident-based (where workers live)

label: Workers who carpooled to work (%)
definition: Workers 16+ who usually carpooled in a car, truck or van as a share of all workers 16+.
breaks: None known for this line
limitations: Large MOEs for small areas; usual mode only

label: Workers commuting by public transportation (%)
definition: Workers 16+ whose usual mode was public transportation (bus, subway, commuter rail, light rail or streetcar, ferry; taxi excluded) as a share of all workers 16+.
breaks: Total line stable; sub-rows _011-_014 relabeled and reordered from the 2015-2019 period; 2024 shells label the line 'Public transportation:'
limitations: Near zero in most rural areas; MOEs large relative to small shares

label: Workers commuting by rail transit (%)
definition: Workers 16+ commuting by subway or elevated rail, long-distance train or commuter rail, or light rail, streetcar or trolley, as a share of all workers 16+.
comparable_span: Sum approximately comparable across the 2019 change; individual lines not comparable
breaks: IDs _012-_014 changed meaning in 2019 (before: streetcar, subway, railroad; after: subway, commuter rail, light rail/streetcar/trolley); category boundaries shifted
limitations: Small counts outside large metros; do not compare individual sub-lines across 2019

label: Workers who walked to work (%)
definition: Workers 16+ who usually walked to work as a share of all workers 16+.
breaks: None known for this line
limitations: Small shares with large relative MOEs; college towns and military bases stand out

label: Workers who bicycled to work (%)
definition: Workers 16+ who usually commuted by bicycle as a share of all workers 16+.
breaks: None known for this line
limitations: Very small shares; MOEs often exceed estimates at tract/BG level

label: Workers who worked from home (%)
definition: Workers 16+ who usually worked from home in the reference week as a share of all workers 16+.
breaks: Label 'Worked at home' through 2014-2018 and 'Worked from home' from 2015-2019; sharp rise in periods including 2020 onward
limitations: Reference-week concept; hybrid workers classified by where they worked most that week

label: Mean travel time to work (minutes)
definition: Aggregate one-way travel time to work of workers 16+ who did not work from home divided by the number of those workers.
universe: Workers 16 years and over who did not work from home
breaks: Aggregate travel time is rounded to the nearest 5 minutes; universe excludes people working from home
limitations: B08013 has no block-group rows (tract is lowest); for custom areas sum aggregates and workers before dividing

label: Workers with one-way commutes of 60+ minutes (%)
definition: Workers 16+ who did not work from home with usual one-way travel time of 60 minutes or more, as a share of all such workers.
universe: Workers 16 years and over who did not work from home
breaks: None known; universe excludes work-from-home
limitations: Self-reported usual travel time; small-area MOEs

label: Households with no vehicle available (%)
definition: Households with no car, van or truck (one-ton or less) kept at home for household use, as a share of all households.
breaks: None known
limitations: B08201 has no block-group rows; for block groups use (B25044_003+B25044_010)/B25044_001

label: Renter households with no vehicle available (%)
definition: Renter-occupied housing units with no vehicle available as a share of all renter-occupied units.
breaks: None known
limitations: Small renter counts in rural block groups produce wide MOEs

label: Average vehicles available per household
definition: Aggregate number of vehicles available divided by occupied housing units.
breaks: None known
limitations: Aggregate is top-coded by the response categories; MOE of a ratio must be approximated

label: Jobs located in the area (all jobs)
definition: Count of all jobs (job type JT00, segment S000) whose workplace census block lies in the area, summed from WAC C000.
universe: Jobs in state UI records plus federal (OPM) employment
breaks: Federal job types from 2010; job frame ages 14-99 from 2012; no WAC files for AK 2017-2023, MI 2022-2023, MA 2002-2010, DC 2002-2009
suppression: State-years without employment data lack WAC files
limitations: Counts jobs, not workers (multiple job holders counted per job); self-employment not covered; report area totals rather than single blocks

label: Jobs paying $1,250 per month or less (%)
definition: WAC jobs with earnings of $1,250 per month or less (CE01) as a share of all jobs (C000) located in the area.
universe: Jobs in state UI records plus federal (OPM) employment
breaks: Earnings bands are fixed nominal thresholds since 2002, so low-earnings shares drift down with wage inflation; same state-year gaps as WAC
suppression: State-years without employment data lack WAC files
limitations: Monthly earnings include part-time and part-month jobs; not an hourly wage measure

label: Jobs located in the area by NAICS sector (%)
definition: WAC jobs in each of 20 NAICS sectors (CNS01-CNS20) as shares of all jobs (C000) located in the area.
universe: Jobs in state UI records plus federal (OPM) employment
breaks: Federal jobs from 2010 raise public administration (CNS20) counts; state-year gaps as WAC
suppression: State-years without employment data lack WAC files
limitations: Sector from employer records; workplace location of multi-establishment employers may be imputed (LEHD method, not verified here)

label: Employed residents (primary jobs held by residents)
definition: Count of primary jobs (JT01) held by workers whose residence block is in the area, from RAC C000; approximates employed residents.
universe: Primary jobs of residents (state UI plus federal employment)
breaks: Federal job types from 2010; RAC for states lacking employment data still includes residents employed in other states
limitations: Self-employed residents not counted; residence locations partly modeled

label: Jobs per employed resident
definition: Primary jobs located in the area (WAC JT01 C000) divided by primary jobs held by area residents (RAC JT01 C000); values above 1 indicate a net importer of workers.
breaks: Missing WAC state-years (AK 2017-2023, MI 2022-2023) make the ratio invalid there
limitations: Sensitive to area size and to missing out-of-state data

label: Employed residents who work in the same area (%)
definition: OD primary jobs (JT01) with both home and work blocks inside the area divided by all primary jobs held by area residents (RAC JT01 C000).
table_or_series: OD {st}_od_main_JT01_{YEAR}.csv.gz (plus other states' aux files for cross-state commuting)
universe: Primary jobs held by area residents
breaks: Missing OD state-years (AK 2017-2023, MI 2022-2023) and 2010 federal-job addition
limitations: Larger areas mechanically retain more workers; cross-state work requires the destination state's aux file

label: Jobs filled by workers living outside the area (%)
definition: OD primary jobs (JT01) with the work block inside the area and the home block outside it, divided by all primary jobs located in the area (WAC JT01 C000).
universe: Primary jobs located in the area
breaks: Missing OD state-years (AK 2017-2023, MI 2022-2023); federal jobs from 2010
limitations: Aux files hold in-state jobs of out-of-state residents; sensitive to area size

label: Motor vehicle traffic deaths
definition: Number of people who died within 30 days of a crash on a trafficway open to the public that occurred in the area (sum of FATALS in accident.csv by STATE and COUNTY of the crash).
universe: Fatal crashes on trafficways customarily open to the public
breaks: Annual Report File values revised in the Final file; GSA county and city codes occasionally split
limitations: Counted where the crash occurred, not where victims lived; small annual counts in small counties (use 3-5 year sums)

label: Traffic deaths per 100,000 residents
definition: FARS deaths from crashes in the area divided by the area's resident population (external Census population estimates) times 100,000.
breaks: As for traffic_fatalities_fars; population denominators change with each estimates vintage
limitations: Numerator by crash location but denominator by residence; unstable for small counties (pool years)

label: Pedestrian and bicyclist traffic deaths
definition: Persons killed (INJ_SEV = 4) whose person type is pedestrian (PER_TYP = 5) or bicyclist (PER_TYP = 6), counted by county of the crash.
comparable_span: 1975-2024 (check person-type code changes in the manual)
breaks: Person-type attribute codes documented by year in the Analytical User's Manual
limitations: Very small counts in most counties; use multi-year sums

label: Households with a broadband subscription of any type (%)
definition: Households with any broadband internet subscription (cellular data plan, cable/fiber/DSL, satellite or other non-dial-up service) as a share of all households.
breaks: 2016 question revision: periods 2013-2017 to 2015-2019 mix old and new wording; Census advises caution comparing pre-2016 data
limitations: Adoption, not availability; group quarters excluded

label: Households with cable, fiber optic or DSL broadband (%)
definition: Households with a broadband subscription such as cable, fiber optic or DSL (alone or with other types) as a share of all households.
breaks: 2016 question revision (see households_broadband_any_share_acs)
limitations: Respondent-reported service type; fixed wireless may be reported inconsistently

label: Households whose only internet subscription is a cellular data plan (%)
definition: Households with a cellular data plan and no other type of internet subscription as a share of all households.
breaks: 2016 revision changed the mobile/cellular category wording
limitations: Indicator of mobile-only connectivity; data caps and speeds not captured

label: Households without an internet subscription (%)
definition: Households with internet access but no subscription plus households with no internet access, as a share of all households.
breaks: 2016 question revision
limitations: Access without subscription includes free public or shared connections

label: Households with no computer (%)
definition: Households reporting no computing device of any type (desktop, laptop, smartphone, tablet or other) as a share of all households.
breaks: 2016 revision changed device categories (smartphone and tablet asked separately)
limitations: Device presence only; working condition and sharing not measured

label: Households whose only computing device is a smartphone (%)
definition: Households with a smartphone and no other type of computing device as a share of all households.
breaks: 2016 revision of device categories
limitations: Captures device dependence, not internet subscription

label: Units with terrestrial fixed broadband of at least 100/20 Mbps (%)
definition: Share of units at broadband serviceable locations in the geography where providers report fixed terrestrial service with maximum advertised speeds of at least 100/20 Mbps.
universe: Units at broadband serviceable locations (Location Fabric)
comparable_span: June 2022 to December 2025 (vintages revised after challenges)
breaks: Not comparable with Form 477 (to June 2021); Fabric versions change each round; summary files restructured (spec v2.4.3)
limitations: Provider-reported advertised speeds; business and residential units combined unless filtered by biz_res; availability, not adoption

label: Units without terrestrial fixed broadband of 25/3 Mbps (%)
definition: One minus the share of units at broadband serviceable locations served by fixed terrestrial technologies at 25/3 Mbps or more.
universe: Units at broadband serviceable locations (Location Fabric)
breaks: Not comparable with Form 477; Fabric and provider revisions between vintages
limitations: Excludes satellite by construction; advertised availability only

label: Population with a fixed terrestrial 25/3 Mbps provider (%, Form 477 legacy)
definition: Population with one or more providers of fixed terrestrial broadband (ADSL, cable, fiber, other copper, fixed wireless; satellite excluded) at 25/3 Mbps, as a share of total population, summing urban/rural and tribal rows.
table_or_series: Area Table (e.g. opendata.fcc.gov xvwq-qtaj for June 2021)
periods: Semiannual December 2016 to June 2021 (Area Tables on opendata.fcc.gov)
breaks: Series ended June 2021; not comparable with BDC; V1/V2 revisions within periods
limitations: Census-block method counts a block as served if one location can be served, overstating coverage

label: Persons who use the internet (%)
definition: Persons age 3+ (not active-duty military) who use the internet at any location, as a share of that population.
universe: Persons age 3+ not in active-duty military
periods: CPS supplement waves Dec 1998 to Nov 2023
breaks: Question wording and universes vary by wave; some metrics marked legacy
limitations: State SEs about 1-2 points; use, not availability; uncertainty value used here means a published survey SE

label: Households where no one uses the internet at home (%)
definition: Households in which no member uses the internet at home, as a share of households (reference persons).
periods: CPS supplement waves Dec 1998 to Nov 2023
breaks: Question wording varies by wave
limitations: State-level only; complements ACS subscription measures

label: Violent crime offenses reported by a police agency
definition: Offenses of murder and nonnegligent manslaughter, rape, robbery and aggravated assault known to the agency (SRS, or NIBRS converted to summary form), summed over months.
universe: Offenses known to law enforcement in the agency's jurisdiction
breaks: 2021 NIBRS-only year left many agencies missing; agency SRS-to-NIBRS transitions change counting rules
suppression: Months an agency did not report are absent or null in API output
limitations: Reported crime only; FBI advises against rankings; agency jurisdictions differ from Census places and can overlap

label: Violent crimes per 100,000 population (agency)
definition: Violent offenses known to the agency divided by the population the FBI assigns to the agency, times 100,000.
breaks: 2021 coverage gap; NIBRS transitions
suppression: Months an agency did not report are absent or null in API output
limitations: FBI discourages rankings; only compare a city to its state and the state to the nation

label: Property crimes per 100,000 population (agency)
definition: Property crime offenses (burglary, larceny-theft, motor vehicle theft; check arson treatment) known to the agency divided by agency population, times 100,000.
breaks: 2021 coverage gap; NIBRS transitions
suppression: Months an agency did not report are absent or null in API output
limitations: Reporting practices for larceny vary; FBI discourages rankings

label: Population covered by agencies reporting to UCR (%)
definition: Percent of the population served by law enforcement agencies that submitted data for the month, as reported by the Crime Data Explorer.
table_or_series: Crime Data API tooltips 'Percent of Population Coverage'
universe: Resident population of the state or nation
breaks: Sharp drop in 2021 (NIBRS-only year): US about 77% vs about 96% in 2020 and 95% in 2022
limitations: Use to flag years where agency counts are incomplete

label: Sworn officers per 1,000 residents (agency)
definition: Sworn law enforcement officers (male plus female officers) reported by the agency divided by the agency's participated population, times 1,000.
universe: Law enforcement employees reported to the UCR Program
periods: Annual (2022-2023 checked; earlier years not verified)
limitations: Agency service population differs from Census geography; sheriffs and state police overlap municipal agencies

label: Violent crimes per 100,000 (county, ICPSR-imputed UCR)
definition: County-aggregated UCR Part I violent offenses (murder, rape, robbery, aggravated assault) including ICPSR imputations, divided by county population, times 100,000.
table_or_series: ICPSR county-level detailed arrest and offense files (crimes reported part), e.g. ICPSR 37059
universe: Offenses known to agencies located in the county
breaks: Imputation method introduced in 1994; series ends with data year 2016
limitations: Imputed values; not official FBI releases; check the Coverage Indicator before use

label: UCR county data Coverage Indicator (ICPSR)
definition: ICPSR diagnostic of the quality of aggregated county UCR data (higher values mean more of the county's data come from complete agency reporting).
table_or_series: ICPSR county-level detailed arrest and offense files
breaks: Introduced with the 1994 method change
limitations: Diagnostic only; use to screen county crime rates

label: Violent victimizations per 1,000 persons age 12+ (national)
definition: Rape or sexual assault, robbery, aggravated assault and simple assault victimizations per 1,000 persons age 12 or older (national NCVS estimate), including crimes not reported to police.
table_or_series: NCVS annual Criminal Victimization estimates / N-DASH
breaks: 2006 methodological changes; 2016 sample redesign; 2024 redesigned instrument reported separately
limitations: National context only; uncertainty value used here means a published survey standard error

label: Fire incidents reported to NFIRS by participating departments
definition: Count of NFIRS incident reports classified as fires (incident type 100 series) submitted by participating fire departments, by department or state.
table_or_series: NFIRS Public Data Release basic incident table
universe: Incidents reported by participating fire departments
breaks: NFIRS 4.1 to 5.0 in 1999; 2025 hybrid NFIRS/NERIS year; NERIS replaces NFIRS from 2026
suppression: Non-participating departments and unreported incidents absent
limitations: USFA: raw NFIRS counts are not a proper measure of total fires or losses; participation varies by year

label: National Risk Index composite risk score
definition: National percentile rank (0-100) of composite natural-hazard risk: Expected Annual Loss adjusted by a community risk factor built from social vulnerability and community resilience.
universe: U.S. counties or census tracts (including territories)
breaks: Each version changes hazards, inputs and methods; v1.20 changed inland flooding, tsunami, landslide and social vulnerability inputs
limitations: Relative rank, not absolute risk; planning-level screening

label: Expected annual loss from natural hazards ($)
definition: Modeled average annual loss to buildings, population (dollar-equivalent) and agriculture from 18 natural hazards.
breaks: Version changes as for nri_risk_score_nri
limitations: Population losses valued as dollar equivalents; tract sums may not equal county values (use published geography)

label: NRI social vulnerability score
definition: National percentile rank of social vulnerability used in the NRI; in v1.20 based on Census Community Resilience Estimates.
breaks: Source changed to Census CRE in v1.20; not comparable with earlier NRI versions
limitations: Relative rank; underlying estimates carry survey error not shown

label: NRI community resilience score
definition: National percentile rank of community resilience from a FEMA-modified version of the HVRI Baseline Resilience Indicators for Communities (2020).
breaks: Based on 2020 BRIC inputs
limitations: Composite of many indicators; relative rank

label: NRI heat wave risk score
definition: National percentile rank of heat wave hazard-type risk (expected annual loss from heat waves adjusted by the community risk factor).
breaks: Heat wave period of record 2005-2024 in v1.20
limitations: Loss-based hazard risk, not a count of hot days

label: Severe weather events recorded (county-based)
definition: Number of Storm Events records with CZ_TYPE = C for the county in a year (zone-based records need an NWS zone-to-county correlation).
universe: Storm Data events reported by NWS offices
breaks: Event types limited before 1996 (tornado only 1950-1954; tornado, thunderstorm wind and hail 1955-1995)
limitations: Counts reflect NWS reporting practice; many winter, heat and flood events are recorded by zone

label: Deaths attributed to storm events
definition: Sum of direct and indirect deaths recorded for storm events located in the county (county-based records; zone records need mapping).
breaks: Event coverage expanded in 1955 and 1996
limitations: Heat and cold deaths often recorded by zone; attribution practices vary

label: Storm event property damage (nominal dollars)
definition: Sum of estimated property damage for storm events in the county after converting K, M and B suffixes to dollars; nominal dollars.
breaks: Event coverage expanded in 1955 and 1996
limitations: Rough estimates, often zero or blank; not insured-loss data; adjust for inflation before comparing years

label: Days with AQI above 100
definition: Days in the year when the county AQI (highest monitor) was 101 or higher: days Unhealthy for Sensitive Groups plus Unhealthy, Very Unhealthy and Hazardous days.
variables: Days Unhealthy for Sensitive Groups;Days Unhealthy;Days Very Unhealthy;Days Hazardous (report column labels; file headers not inspected)
universe: Days with AQI in counties with monitors
comparable_span: Check AQI definition changes before long comparisons
breaks: SO2 excluded from county/CBSA AQI summaries from December 8, 2021; AQI breakpoints revised over time; PM2.5 data advisory on recent files
limitations: Driven by the worst monitor; number of monitored days varies by county and year

label: Median daily AQI
definition: Median of the county's daily AQI values for the year (half of days at or below this value).
variables: Median AQI (report label AQI Median; file header not inspected)
universe: Days with AQI in counties with monitors
comparable_span: Check AQI definition changes before long comparisons
breaks: SO2 excluded from summaries from December 8, 2021; breakpoint revisions
limitations: Pollutants monitored differ by county; not population-weighted

label: PM2.5 national percentile (EJScreen 2024, archived)
definition: National percentile of the block group's annual average PM2.5 concentration (tract values from EPA monitor and CMAQ model fusion assigned to block groups).
breaks: EPA discontinued EJScreen in February 2025; indicator years and methods differ between versions
limitations: Screening-level exposure proxy from an unofficial archive; not a risk measure

label: Traffic proximity national percentile (EJScreen 2024, archived)
definition: National percentile of traffic proximity and volume: annual average daily traffic at major roads divided by distance (2020 HPMS).
breaks: EPA discontinued EJScreen in February 2025
limitations: Proxy for exposure to traffic; archived unofficial copy

label: Extreme heat days, May-September (CDC Tracking)
definition: Annual number of extreme heat days from May to September based on modeled daily temperatures (Tracking measure 423; threshold as defined in CDC indicator documentation).
breaks: Full-year version is a separate measure (ID 1427)
limitations: Relative, locally defined threshold; modeled data; API throttles non-token use

label: Area in severe drought or worse (%)
definition: Percent of county area in U.S. Drought Monitor category D2 (severe) or worse; weekly values, commonly averaged over a year.
breaks: None documented; statisticsType 1 is cumulative and 2 is categorical
limitations: Expert-blended weekly assessment; area-based (population-based variant available)

label: Developed land share (%)
definition: Share of 30 m pixels in the area classified as developed (NLCD classes 21-24: open space, low, medium and high intensity) in Annual NLCD land cover.
universe: Land-cover pixels in the area (conterminous U.S.)
breaks: Each collection reprocesses the full series (use one collection); legacy NLCD epochs are not directly comparable
limitations: Classification error; developed open space includes parks and large lawns; CONUS only

label: Mean impervious surface (%)
definition: Average fractional impervious surface across 30 m pixels in the area (Annual NLCD Fractional Impervious Surface product).
breaks: Collections reprocess the full series
limitations: Modeled pixel fractions; CONUS only

label: Democratic share of the presidential vote (%)
definition: Votes for the Democratic presidential candidate divided by total presidential votes in the county.
universe: Ballots with a vote for president
breaks: Check Alaska (districts) and Connecticut (Census planning regions from 2022) before joining to Census counties
limitations: Verify column names and any vote-mode rows in the gated 2000-2024 file before summing

label: Republican share of the presidential vote (%)
definition: Votes for the Republican presidential candidate divided by total presidential votes in the county.
universe: Ballots with a vote for president
breaks: As for presidential_vote_share_dem_medsl
limitations: As for presidential_vote_share_dem_medsl

label: Total votes cast for president
definition: Total votes for president (all candidates) in the county.
universe: Ballots with a vote for president
breaks: Legacy codebook notes Alaska 2004 district returns overstate votes
limitations: Excludes ballots with no presidential vote (undervotes)

label: Presidential turnout as % of citizen voting-age population
definition: Total votes for president divided by the citizen voting-age population (ACS CVAP 5-year estimate ending in the election year), times 100.
table_or_series: countypres_2000-2024 plus CVAP special tabulation County.csv
breaks: Earliest CVAP release is 2005-2009, so 2012 is the first year with an ending-year match
limitations: Denominator is a 5-year average; numerator excludes undervotes; CVAP ignores other eligibility limits

label: Citizens 18+ reporting they were registered (%)
definition: Percent of U.S. citizens age 18+ who reported being registered to vote in the November election (CPS supplement).
table_or_series: Table 4a (vote04a_{YEAR}.xlsx); historical Tables A-5a/A-5b and A-3b
periods: November of even years; state tables from 1972 (presidential) and 1974 (congressional)
breaks: Compare presidential with presidential and midterm with midterm years
limitations: Self-reported and overstated; state-level only; uncertainty value used here means a published CPS margin of error

label: Citizens 18+ reporting they voted (%)
definition: Percent of U.S. citizens age 18+ who reported voting in the November election (CPS supplement).
table_or_series: Table 4a (vote04a_{YEAR}.xlsx); historical Tables A-5a/A-5b and A-3a
periods: November of even years; state tables from 1972 (presidential) and 1974 (congressional)
breaks: Compare like election types
limitations: Self-reports exceed official turnout; state-level only

label: Active registered voters as % of citizen voting-age population
definition: Active registrations reported by the election jurisdiction (A1b) divided by the citizen voting-age population, times 100.
comparable_span: Check item definitions for each cycle
breaks: Jurisdiction types differ by state (towns in WI and New England); list-maintenance practices differ
suppression: Codes -88 (does not apply) and -99 (data not available)
limitations: Can exceed 100% because rolls include movers; town jurisdictions need MCD-level CVAP (12 states only)

label: Voters who voted by mail (%)
definition: Mail votes (F1d) as a share of total voters participating in the general election (F1a).
universe: Voters participating in the general election
comparable_span: Check item definitions for each cycle
breaks: Mode categories and definitions changed across cycles
suppression: Codes -88 and -99; in 2024 F1d valid for 6,133 of 6,461 jurisdictions
limitations: Missing modes in some jurisdictions; state vote-by-mail laws drive levels

label: Residents who volunteered through an organization (%)
definition: Share of state residents covered by the CEV who volunteered with an organization at least once in the 12 months before the September survey.
universe: Civilian noninstitutional population covered by the CEV
breaks: Pre-2017 volunteer supplements are a different series; 2021 wave collected during the pandemic
suppression: No SEs in the open-data table
limitations: Modest state samples; no uncertainty published in this table

label: Residents who report voting in local elections (%)
definition: Share of state residents reporting voting in local elections (CEV measure 'voting in local elections'; see CEV documentation for response coding).
universe: Civilian noninstitutional population covered by the CEV
breaks: As for formal_volunteering_rate_cev
suppression: No SEs in the open-data table
limitations: Self-reported; question coding not verified here

label: Citizen voting-age population
definition: Estimated U.S. citizens age 18+ (CVAP_EST, total line) from the ACS 5-year CVAP special tabulation.
table_or_series: CVAP special tabulation (Nation, State, County, Place, MCD, Tract, BlockGr, CD, SLDUC, SLDLC csv)
breaks: Tract and block-group boundary vintages change with the decennial census; MCD file only for 12 states
limitations: Rounded estimates; MOEs large for small areas

label: Local government property tax revenue per capita
definition: Property tax revenue (item T01, in $000) of local governments divided by population; for a county area sum all local units located there (complete only in census years ending in 2 and 7).
universe: Local governments (counties, municipalities, townships, special districts, school districts)
periods: Annual fiscal years; full universe in census years (2022, 2017, ...)
comparable_span: Census years at 5-year intervals; annual for certainty units
breaks: Sample vs census years; unit ID change (PID to GID); fiscal-year timing differs across governments
limitations: Census cautions that unit data are not an accurate time series; sample years omit many small governments; overlapping governments complicate area totals

label: Local government tax revenue per capita
definition: Sum of all tax item codes (codes beginning with T, e.g. T01 property, T09 general sales, T40 individual income) for local governments divided by population.
variables: all item codes beginning with T;Population (PID file)
periods: Annual fiscal years; full universe in census years
breaks: As for local_gov_property_tax_per_capita_govfin
limitations: Tax assignment follows the collecting government; state-local responsibility splits differ by state

label: Local government long-term debt outstanding per capita
definition: Long-term debt outstanding at the end of the fiscal year (item 49U, in $000) divided by population.
periods: Annual fiscal years; full universe in census years
breaks: Debt item detail differs in older classification versions
limitations: Special-district debt may serve residents outside the county

label: Police protection current operations spending per capita
definition: Police protection current operation expenditure (item E62, in $000) of local governments divided by population.
periods: Annual fiscal years; full universe in census years
breaks: As for local_gov_property_tax_per_capita_govfin
limitations: Excludes capital outlay; county sheriff and municipal police split varies

label: Full-time local government employees per 1,000 residents
definition: Full-time employees across all functions (item code 000) divided by the government's population, times 1,000; sum units for an area in census years.
universe: Government employees in the March pay period
breaks: Sample vs census years; new unit ID from the 2021 revision (May 2024)
limitations: Not FTE; the ID-file population field holds enrollment for school districts and a function code for special districts

label: Current spending per pupil (school district)
definition: Total current expenditures for elementary and secondary education (TCURELSC) divided by fall membership (V33).
periods: Annual FY1990-FY2022 at NCES (FY2024 via Census elsec files)
breaks: Sample-only years FY1991, FY1993 and FY1994; nominal dollars
limitations: Nominal dollars; charter and non-geographic LEAs; regional cost differences

label: School district revenue by source (federal, state, local %)
definition: Federal (TFEDREV), state (TSTREV) and local (TLOCREV) revenue as shares of total revenue (TOTALREV = TFEDREV + TSTREV + TLOCREV).
periods: Annual FY1990-FY2022 at NCES (FY2024 via Census elsec files)
breaks: Sample-only years FY1991, FY1993 and FY1994; one-time federal programs can shift shares in individual years
limitations: State aid formulas differ; pass-through federal aid counted as federal

label: Public library visits per capita
definition: Annual library visits (VISITS) divided by legal service area population (POPU_LSA) for the library system.
breaks: Imputation methods changed FY2006-FY2008 (IMLS bridge study)
suppression: -3 for temporarily closed libraries; imputed values flagged
limitations: Legal service areas do not match Census geographies exactly; visitors include non-residents

label: Public library operating expenditures per capita
definition: Total operating expenditures (TOTOPEXP) divided by legal service area population (POPU_LSA).
breaks: Imputation changes FY2006-FY2008
suppression: Staff expenditure detail set to -9 when total FTE is 2.00 or less (total operating expenditures unaffected)
limitations: Nominal dollars; system-level finance

label: Public library outlets (central, branch, bookmobile)
definition: Number of central libraries, branches and bookmobiles reported by library systems (CENTLIB + BRANLIB + BKMOB), or a count of records in the outlet file.
breaks: Outlet type definitions refined over time
limitations: Outlet file includes temporarily closed outlets flagged by structure code

label: General revenue per capita, fiscally standardized city
definition: General revenue raised by or for the central city FiSC (city plus allocated shares of overlying county, school and special district revenue) per resident, in real dollars.
breaks: Dollar base year ambiguous (About sheet says 2022 dollars; cpi equals 1 in 2023 rows); allocation methods per Lincoln working paper
limitations: Large cities only; allocations are estimates; Lincoln Terms of Service limit reuse
